verdict.rationale: Gmail's own documentation describes filters: account-level rules that evaluate incoming messages against criteria such as sender, subject or size, and automatically add or remove labels or forward the email when a message matches. Users can also build a filter directly from search-operator results. Push notifications only let a developer's own backend react to mailbox changes, so they are not credited as user-defined rules. Missing for 10: documented triggers beyond incoming-message matching, a broader action set than labeling and forwarding, any AI or Gemini-driven rule automation (Gemini actions are on-demand only), and independent or hands-on corroboration.
